data.completion_memo: Made the Chat-history sort unit-independent. `sortable_time` in desktop/src-tauri/src/runtime/history.rs now normalises any epoch-seconds label to milliseconds before comparing (labels below EPOCH_MILLISECOND_CEILING = 1e11 are multiplied by 1000 with saturating_mul), so the sort no longer depends on whether `history::now_label` (seconds) or `run_events::now_label` (milliseconds) stamped the newest event of a Chat. Malformed labels still sort to 0 and never panic. This fixes already-persisted mixed-unit streams without a migration. Verified with the new focused unit test `runtime::history::tests::sortable_time_orders_seconds_and_milliseconds_on_one_scale` (cargo test --lib sortable_time: 1 passed). Note: one unrelated pre-existing test, runtime::service::comfyui::tests::fallback_ids_are_identifier_safe_and_bounded, fails on Linux because it hard-codes a Windows path; it is untouched by this task.

lines:
Symptom: the Chat history list is not always newest-first.
Root cause (researched): `history_entries` sorts by `sortable_time(summary.updated_at)` descending (`desktop/src-tauri/src/runtime/history.rs:1666-1687`; helper at 2473-2475 parses the label as u64). `summary.updated_at` comes from `LocalHistoryStore::latest_event_time` (crates/aworkit-local-store/src/ledger/queries.rs:7-21), i.e. the `createdAt` of the highest-sequence event. `createdAt` is written in two different units into the same stream: seconds by `history.rs::now_label` (2342-2347) and milliseconds by `run_events.rs::now_label` (1407-1412). A 13-digit millisecond label always outranks a 10-digit second label, so rows jump positions depending on which producer wrote the newest event.
Fix: make ordering unit-independent. Normalise the label in the sort path so epoch seconds and epoch milliseconds compare correctly (and keep the tie-break stable). Fix the shared label producer so new events use one unit. Keep the change backward compatible with already-persisted streams.
Verification: focused Rust unit test for the comparator/`sortable_time` covering seconds, milliseconds and unparseable labels; run only the affected crate's tests.

data.title: Fix Chat history ordering: normalise the mixed createdAt units the sort key compares
